children: RBC Wealth Management, a division of Royal Bank of Canada, has recruited a large financial advisor team in Pennsylvania. The Nepa/Susco Team has joined RBC's Pittsburgh North branch from UBS, where it advised on more than $1 billion in client assets.

The five-person team works with high- and ultrahigh-net-worth families and individuals, including business executives, advising on areas such as investment management and retirement and estate planning.

The team includes Raymond Nepa, a managing director, who broke into the industry in 1982 and joined UBS in 1995, and Jennifer Susco, also a managing director, who first registered as a broker with UBS in 2007.

Julia Munchel, an 11-year industry veteran, is the third advisor on the team. The practice also includes Karen Venneri, a senior investment associate, and client associate Max Freed. Susco and Munchel are Certified Financial Planners.
A spokeswoman for UBS declined to comment on the departure.
Frank Albanese, director of RBC's Great Lakes Complex, lauded the Nepa/Susco practice for a far-reaching and team-oriented approach in its work with clients.

"What stood out to the Nepa/Susco Team about RBC was the genuine culture of collaboration, having decision makers close at hand, and the sheer breadth of resources they can tap into for their clients," he says. "We're eager to help this team build on what they've already accomplished."

RBC has become an aggressive recruiter as it looks to build out its U.S. wealth operations. It has lured many large advisor teams away from large brokerage firms and is also recruiting senior managers.

On Friday, the day after announcing the addition of the Nepa/Susco practice, RBC said it had hired Shawn Bernhard from Raymond James to serve as complex director for the Texas South region, where she will oversee advisors in Texas and Louisiana. Bernhard, who has more than 25 years of industry experience, is a Certified Financial Planner and held a variety of leadership roles at UBS before joining Raymond James in 2025.
Raymond James didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on Bernhard's departure.
